name: Aditya Agarwal
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Facebook in summer 2005 as one of its first engineers (age ~22–23), built the platform's early search engine at Mark Zuckerberg's direction, and by age 24 was managing engineers, later becoming Facebook's first Director of Product Engineering.
early_history_summary: Born in India to a chemical-engineer father and homemaker mother, Agarwal moved frequently across Cameroon, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand before the U.S. He taught himself programming from books after getting a home computer around age 11–12, completed CMU BS and fifth-year MS in computer science, briefly worked at Oracle, then joined early Facebook in 2005 and owned major product-engineering scope before co-founding Cove (acquired by Dropbox) and serving as Dropbox CTO.
secondary_engine: Scarce technical depth; structural wave (social platforms)
family_context_summary: Born in India; father was a chemical engineer whose work moved the family across Africa and Southeast Asia; mother was a homemaker. Family later immigrated to the United States.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's engineering career and willingness to buy a home computer supported early technical exposure; no documented software-industry inheritance.
primary_early_advantage_tags: CMU CS, early Facebook, Zuckerberg challenge, immigrant mobility, self-taught coding
evidence_summary: Agarwal combined early self-taught programming, a compressed CMU CS BS+MS path, and a 2005 move into Facebook's first ~15 engineers, where Zuckerberg tasked him with search on day two and he later became first Director of Product Engineering. CMU and LA Times profiles corroborate age (~22–23 at join) and the search mandate; Wikipedia and TechCrunch cover Cove acquisition and Dropbox CTO tenure. Family engineering exposure and frequent international moves appear as mild early conditions; elite school plus early Facebook network dominate the advantage stack.
starting_point: Born 1982 in India to a chemical-engineer father and homemaker mother; childhood spent moving across Cameroon, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand before U.S. immigration.
current_position: General partner at South Park Commons; former CTO of Dropbox and early Facebook Director of Product Engineering.

trajectory.event: Completed accelerated CMU computer science bachelor's and fifth-year master's; briefly worked at Oracle in Silicon Valley.
Joined Facebook as one of its first engineers and built the platform's early search engine under Mark Zuckerberg's direction.
Began managing Facebook engineers and scaled into product-engineering leadership for core products.
Left Facebook after serving as first Director of Product Engineering; co-founded collaboration startup Cove with Ruchi Sanghvi.
Cove acquired by Dropbox; joined Dropbox as VP of Engineering.
Appointed CTO of Dropbox, succeeding co-founder Arash Ferdowsi.
Left Dropbox to join South Park Commons as a partner/investor with Sanghvi.
